\section[il torneo]{il torneo — tournament}

\label{lesson:IT-C512-torneo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for league table, then the Italian for to knock out.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il torneo}
\textbf{il torneo} — \textquotedblleft{}tournament\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
A giugno c'è il torneo di tennis della scuola.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{In June there is the school tennis tournament.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Vincere un torneo} — to win a tournament.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{torneo} comes from Old French \emph{tornei} \textquotedblleft{}a tournament\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{torner} \textquotedblleft{}to turn\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{tornāre} \textquotedblleft{}to turn on a lathe\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il torneo}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il torneo}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{il torneo}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for league table, then the Italian for to knock out, then say \emph{il torneo} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does il torneo mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Tournament\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[la semifinale]{la semifinale — semi-final}

\label{lesson:IT-C512-semifinale}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to knock out, then the Italian for tournament.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la semifinale}
\textbf{la semifinale} — \textquotedblleft{}semi-final\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Abbiamo perso in semifinale.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We lost in the semi-final.}
\end{quote}

The plural is \emph{le semifinali}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{semifinale} is built from Latin \emph{sēmi-} \textquotedblleft{}half\textquotedblright{} and \emph{finale}, from \emph{fīnis} \textquotedblleft{}end\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for to knock out, then the Italian for tournament, then say \emph{la semifinale} again

\section[qualificarsi]{qualificarsi — to qualify}

\label{lesson:IT-C512-qualificarsi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for tournament, then the Italian for semi-final.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: qualificarsi}
\textbf{qualificarsi} — \textquotedblleft{}to qualify\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Se vinciamo domani, ci qualifichiamo per la finale.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{If we win tomorrow, we qualify for the final.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Qualificarsi per} — to qualify for.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{qualificarsi} comes from Medieval Latin \emph{quālificāre} \textquotedblleft{}to give a quality\textquotedblright{}, built on Latin \emph{quālis} \textquotedblleft{}of what kind\textquotedblright{} and \emph{facere} \textquotedblleft{}to make\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[la medaglia]{la medaglia — medal}

\label{lesson:IT-C512-medaglia}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for semi-final, then the Italian for to qualify.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la medaglia}
\textbf{la medaglia} — \textquotedblleft{}medal\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ha vinto la medaglia d'oro.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{She won the gold medal.}
\end{quote}

\emph{D'oro}, \emph{d'argento}, \emph{di bronzo}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{medaglia} is usually traced to Vulgar Latin \emph{metallea} \textquotedblleft{}of metal\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB lists \emph{medalia}), from Latin \emph{metallum} \textquotedblleft{}metal\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[il podio]{il podio — podium}

\label{lesson:IT-C512-podio}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to qualify, then the Italian for medal.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il podio}
\textbf{il podio} — \textquotedblleft{}podium\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Sono salita sul podio per la prima volta.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I stood on the podium for the first time.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Salire sul podio} — to finish in the top three.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{podio} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{podium} \textquotedblleft{}a raised platform\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from Greek \emph{pódion} \textquotedblleft{}a little foot, a base\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
